reply: Guided tour of WISE 0855-0714: 6 steps. Touch any control to take over.

steps.say: This is WISE 0855-0714: Coldest known brown dwarf (Y type), about 2.3 pc away. SPHEREx imaged it on 3 dates in D5, from 2025-05-06 to 2026-05-01 (360 days). The view starts on D5 (3.83–4.41 µm).

Play the dates in order. At 8.1″/yr it should move about 1.3 px (pixels are 6.2″) between the first and last date; the crosshair marks where the catalog motion puts it on each date. Measured between 2025-05-06 and 2025-11-12, the dates where it is bright enough to fit: 0.67 px, against 0.7 px expected for that interval.
Blink compares two dates directly: 2025-05-06 against 2026-05-01. A moving source jumps; a still one only changes brightness, if at all.

The six detectors cover 0.75–5.0 µm, from left to right. In the measurements it is detected in D5, D6 and not in D1, D2, D3, D4. Its D5/D4 flux ratio (methane index) is at least 10.6; ordinary stars sit near 0.5–1.5 and methane-rich cold dwarfs far above.
The model motor-rf-E_servible_binario-spherex-2026-11-16T0256 labels it a candidate cold brown dwarf; that agrees with the catalog type (cold brown dwarf, SIMBAD).
4 of 33 sources in this field need a human look. The first one, CWISE J085505.62-071320.6, is flagged for: Only in one date; No Gaia counterpart. Is it real or an artefact?
